messages.subject: Error with truncate function T(....,0,Inf)
parts:
Hi All,

I have been trying to implement a nimbleModel, but there seems to be an issue that is popping out with regards to the truncate function. The following is my code:

dat <- read.csv("3He3Hedat.csv")
re <- as.numeric(dat$lab) # Change the label to a numeric vector
# Note that the numbers are assigned by "sorting" the labels in alphabetical order
Nre <- length(unique(dat$lab))
# Unique removes duplicated vector, we want to know how many groups of 
# data are there
N <- nrow(dat) # Total No of data sets
obsy <- dat$S    # Response variable in MeV
obsx <-  dat$E   # Predictors
erry <- dat$Stat # Error in MeV
set <- dat$lab # Get the labels as a vector

# Inputting the quoted systematic uncertainty:
syst = c(log(1.057),log(1.082),log(1.037),log(1.045),log(1.038))
# In accordance to 
# 1 Bon99 5.7%
# 2 Daw71 8.2%
# 3 Jun98 3.7%
# 4 Kra87 4.5%
# 5 Kud04 3.8%
samplerCode <-  nimbleCode({
  for (i in 1:N) {
    mut[i] <- (exp(2.429819509 * i.screen * (obsx[i]^(-1.5)))) * 
      (alpha + beta * obsx[i] + gamma * (obsx[i]^2))
    yt[i] <- y.norm[re[i]]*mut[i]
    # Temp mean (mut) multiplied by normalising constant, 
    ya[i] ~ dnorm(yt[i],sd = y.scat[re[i]])
    # re[i] refers to the index that we would use to refer to the category
    obsy[i] ~ dnorm(ya[i], sd = erry[i])
    # Propagating the errors in observations of y
  }
  ## PRIORS  
  ### polynomial parameters
  alpha ~ T(dnorm(0.0,sd=100),0,Inf)
  # Note the difference in how we truncate the distributions
  beta ~ dnorm(0.0,sd=100)
  gamma ~ dnorm(0.0,sd=100)
  i.screen ~ T(dnorm(0.0,sd=100),0,Inf)  
  # Some sort of hyperprior for the "grand mean"
  mt ~ T(dnorm(0.0,sd=5),0,Inf)
  for (k in 1:Nre){
    # Systematic Uncertainty as a highly informative prior
    y.norm[k] ~ dlnorm(log(1.0),sd = syst[k])
    y.scat[k] ~ T(dnorm(mt,sd=100),0,Inf)
  }
})

samplerData <- list(obsy = obsy,    # Response variable
                    obsx = obsx   # Predictors
                     )

samplerConst <- list(N = N, # Sample size
                    Nre = Nre, 
                    re = re, # This is used to "iterate")
                    erry = erry,
                    syst = syst
                    )

samplerInits <- list(alpha = 1, 
                     beta = -1, 
                     gamma = 1, 
                     i.screen = 1e-6
                     )

ourmodel <- nimbleModel(code = samplerCode, constants = samplerConst,
                        data = samplerData, inits = samplerInits, check = FALSE
                        ,name = "3He3He")


The required csv file is attached. 

Surprisingly, if I were to change  y.scat[k] ~ T(dnorm(mt,sd=100),0,Inf)  to    y.scat[k] ~ dnorm(0,sd=100) and remove mt, the code works fine! So I'm guesing the problem stems from the T() function. The following shows the error output from R when I tried to run this code:

defining model...
building model...
setting data and initial values...
running calculate on model (any error reports that follow may simply reflect missing values in model variables) ... Error in if (0 <= model$mt[1] & model$mt[1] <= Inf) model$logProb_mt[1] <<- dnorm(model$mt[1],  : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

Any idea how I can try to mitigate this error? Thanks!

HK Tan (Hong Kiat Tan),
Undergraduate Student | Physics 
National University of Singapore

parts:
HK, I've taken a look at your model.  Fortunately there were no serious errors here, it just boiled down to improper model initialization.

I've added initial values for mt, ya, y.norm, and y.scat.  Everything works fine now, and I've taken your model through to building, compiling, and running an MCMC.

See the modified code below.  Please look through the code for comments beginning with "DT", which give a few more details.

Let us know if you have any more questions!

Cheers,
Daniel
NIMBLE development team


library(nimble)

dat <- read.csv("3He3Hedat.csv")

re <- as.numeric(dat$lab) # Change the label to a numeric vector

## Note that the numbers are assigned by "sorting" the labels in alphabetical order

Nre <- length(unique(dat$lab))
## Unique removes duplicated vector, we want to know how many groups of
## data are there

N <- nrow(dat) # Total No of data sets
obsy <- dat$S    # Response variable in MeV
obsx <-  dat$E   # Predictors
erry <- dat$Stat # Error in MeV
set <- dat$lab # Get the labels as a vector

## Inputting the quoted systematic uncertainty:
syst = c(log(1.057),log(1.082),log(1.037),log(1.045),log(1.038))
                                        ## In accordance to
                                        ## 1 Bon99 5.7%
                                        ## 2 Daw71 8.2%
                                        ## 3 Jun98 3.7%
                                        ## 4 Kra87 4.5%
                                        ## 5 Kud04 3.8%

samplerCode <-  nimbleCode({
    for (i in 1:N) {
        mut[i] <- (exp(2.429819509 * i.screen * (obsx[i]^(-1.5)))) * (alpha + beta * obsx[i] + gamma * (obsx[i]^2))
        yt[i] <- y.norm[re[i]]*mut[i]
## Temp mean (mut) multiplied by normalising constant,
ya[i] ~ dnorm(yt[i],sd = y.scat[re[i]])
## re[i] refers to the index that we would use to refer to the category
obsy[i] ~ dnorm(ya[i], sd = erry[i])
## Propagating the errors in observations of y

}
    ## PRIORS  
    ## polynomial parameters
    alpha ~ T(dnorm(0.0,sd=100),0,Inf)
## Note the difference in how we truncate the distributions

beta ~ dnorm(0.0,sd=100)
    gamma ~ dnorm(0.0,sd=100)
    i.screen ~ T(dnorm(0.0,sd=100),0,Inf)
## Some sort of hyperprior for the "grand mean"

mt ~ T(dnorm(0.0,sd=5),0,Inf)
    for (k in 1:Nre){

## Systematic Uncertainty as a highly informative prior
        y.norm[k] ~ dlnorm(0,sd = syst[k])       ## DT: changed log(1.0) to 0

y.scat[k] ~ T(dnorm(mt,sd=100),0,Inf)
    }
})
samplerData <- list(obsy = obsy)    # Response variable

samplerConst <- list(N = N, # Sample size
                     Nre = Nre,
                     re = re, # This is used to "iterate")
                     erry = erry,

syst = syst,
                     obsx = obsx     # Predictors   ## DT: moved predictor/covariate obsx to "constants",
                                                    ## more appropriate than "data", although if you plan
                                                    ## on ever changing the values of obsx, then move it back to "data"

)

samplerInits <- list(alpha = 1,
                     beta = -1,
                     gamma = 1,

i.screen = 1e-6,
                     mt = 1,                  ## DT: initial value added
                     ya = rep(1, N),          ## DT: initial value added
                     y.norm = rep(1, Nre),    ## DT: initial value added
                     y.scat = rep(1, Nre)     ## DT: initial value added
                     )

ourmodel <- nimbleModel(samplerCode, samplerConst, samplerData, samplerInits)

Rmodel <- ourmodel

Rmodel$calculate()     ## DT: -34550.91  good, a real number.  model is now fully initialized

conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel)
conf$printSamplers(byType = TRUE)
conf$printMonitors()
Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)

Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)

set.seed(0)
samples <- runMCMC(Cmcmc, 10000)

library(basicMCMCplots)
samplesPlot(samples, c('alpha', 'beta', 'gamma'))
samplesPlot(samples, 'y.norm')

samplesSummary(samples)
